results.reasoning: Re-judged after 04894f81 (n-0617). Driven with Playwright on a scratch copy of the cli blueprint served from its own home on port 4766, its run records retargeted to that port so topher signatures count, and by calling sinceSigned() read-only on the eight real cli rules topher signed on older wordings: all eight find the signed wording and every one now carries its reasons, including ownership.design.proposed-version-exists, whose Oct 20 reason after an Oct 19 (Chicago) signature was the one dropped before. Each step holds: the block sits above detail.turn and says the rule changed since you signed it on your signature day in your zone; with the copy given its own git history it lists reworded steps with the words that went struck through and those that came marked, and added steps (removed proven on a fixture through stepChanges); the dated reasons stand beneath; outside git it says the wording you signed is no longer on record and still shows the reasons; a reader who never signed, and a rule signed on its current wording, show nothing; the request carries the reader own signature hash. Edges weighed: a day-only reason still compares in UTC, so one written the same evening as a signature made after 19:00 Chicago and dated by the local day is dropped, and one written earlier on a signature day now shows as since it; both estimated 10-20% and reported to the dispatcher, not filed.
